clue.text: Settlement of conflict is in hand

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the outer word

parts.note: a hand of cards is the deal you are given
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: A dispute that has been brought under control and is close to being resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests ending a dispute, but here it means paying a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrayal is the paying of costs, which is the settlement of a bill or account.

clue.text: Honest conduct

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to manage or guide, as with an orchestra

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a noun phrase about good behaviour, but 'conduct' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for frank, plain speaking and a verb meaning to manage or steer something.

clue.text: In appearance the Italian is slick

indicators.note: the Italian word sits inside the word for appearance

parts.note: a face is an outward appearance, as in 'on the face of it'
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: Judging by looks, the Italian man is a smooth operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes something glib or superficially easy, much like slick talk or a slick performance.

clue.text: A footballer stores new canopy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so the player's word holds the other letter

parts.note: a wing is a footballer playing on the flank
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A football player keeps a brand-new shelter in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a shopfront or window as a shelter, a kind of canopy.

clue.text: Festival permits touring stately home

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: permits as a verb
many English stately homes are called a Hall

explanation.surface: An event's organisers give permission for a tour round a grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL HALLOWS is All Saints' Day, 1 November, whose eve is Halloween.
explanation.definitionFit: All Hallows is the Christian feast of All Saints, a church festival held on the first of November.

clue.text: MP died during summing up

indicators.note: something happening during another is set within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a recap is a summary
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament collapsed and died while closing a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: MP here is military police, not a Member of Parliament; a redcap is a British military policeman, named for the red cap cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cover worn on the cap, and MP abbreviates military police.

clue.text: Rowing team without a word of consent makes sense

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the crew's word wraps round the other

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers
the word said to agree

explanation.surface: A rowing crew that never agrees on anything is talking good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one of the five bodily senses along with hearing and touch.

clue.text: Fastening holds up trunk of tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece holding up another sits beneath it, so the fastening comes last

parts.note: a trunk is a large chest for storage
a nut fastens onto a bolt

explanation.surface: A clip supports the trunk of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk of tree' reads as one phrase, but the trunk is a storage box and the tree is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The chestnut is a broadleaf tree, either the sweet chestnut or the horse chestnut that drops conkers.

clue.text: Dressed-up street traders have nobleman tucking into tarts

indicators.note: something tucking into another goes inside it, so the noble's title goes inside

parts.note: tarts and pies are pastry dishes
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Costumed market sellers watch a lord tuck into their pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: The pearlies are London's Pearly Kings and Queens, costermongers (street traders) whose clothes are covered in pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearlies are London costermongers who wear outfits sewn with mother-of-pearl buttons, so they are costumed street sellers.

clue.text: Money put in bank not long ago

indicators.note: money put in somewhere is placed inside it

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
a cent is a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone deposited cash in their bank account a short while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun for a place to put money, but it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time just past, so it is an adverb of the same sense as the phrase.

clue.text: Dramatist rewrites a scene

indicators.note: rewriting a passage puts its material into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A playwright redrafts one episode of his play.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a Roman Stoic philosopher who wrote tragedies, so he was a dramatist.

clue.text: Stop to mention an island

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark, a stop
to say is to mention

explanation.surface: Someone pauses in conversation to bring up an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonsay is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is one of the Inner Hebrides of Scotland, a small inhabited island near Oronsay.

clue.text: Capriciously spoilt Shakespearean role

indicators.note: acting capriciously means unpredictably, so the letters fall in no fixed order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor playing a Shakespeare part behaves like a pampered, whimsical child.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistol is the swaggering companion of Falstaff in Henry IV Part 2, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Decent reason for public entertainment

definitions.note: a fairground is the site of the entertainment rather than the entertainment itself

parts.note: fair means reasonable or decent
grounds are reasons, as in 'on what ground?'

explanation.surface: A sound justification is offered for staging a show for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is the open site where a funfair with rides and stalls is set up for people to enjoy.

clue.text: Battered hake dropped into girl's top? That's novel!

indicators.note: dropping something into a garment puts it inside

parts.note: a blouse is a woman's top

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the fish's letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of fried fish in batter has fallen down a girl's top, which is a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' plays on fish in batter; 'novel' looks like 'new' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, published in serial parts in 1852 and 1853.

clue.text: Col. Bates demolished barrier

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts lie in disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A colonel named Bates knocked down a fence or blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is anything standing in the way and preventing progress, just as a barrier blocks passage.

clue.text: Manager protects a number showing emaciation

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it

parts.note: a boss is a manager
any number may be chosen; this one fits

explanation.surface: A team manager shields one of his players, who looks dreadfully thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Boniness is the state of being so thin that the bones stand out, which is what emaciation means.

clue.text: Recommend against commander breaking a tryst

indicators.note: something breaking into another splits it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a tryst is a date, a romantic meeting
V for versus
OC is officer commanding

explanation.surface: Advising an officer not to keep a secret lovers' meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course is to speak publicly in favour of it, which is to recommend it.

clue.text: An American woman's promise is a dangerous thing

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
the possessive ending
giving your word is promising

explanation.surface: A warning that a pledge from a certain American lady can't be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy, wide-bladed cutting sword, plainly a weapon that can do real harm.

clue.text: Holy man gets widespread support for violent struggle

indicators.note: in a down entry a support goes underneath, so the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
rife means widespread, common

explanation.surface: A cleric wins broad backing for an armed uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter conflict or fighting, so it names a violent struggle between people or groups.

clue.text: In Scottish island measure gas

indicators.note: the measure is placed in the island's name

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: Someone measures gas on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Butene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas, an alkene with four carbon atoms used in making plastics.

clue.text: Decay found in grain? Get away!

indicators.note: something found in another lies inside it

parts.note: a grain is a tiny bit
to eat away is to corrode or decay

explanation.surface: Rot discovered in stored corn, and a cry to shoo someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is an informal command telling someone to go away, the same as shouting 'Get away!'

clue.text: Get high before big exams

indicators.note: one piece coming before another is placed first in the answer

parts.note: to trip is to be high on a hallucinogenic drug
OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation

explanation.surface: A student takes drugs ahead of major examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big exams' reads as one phrase, but 'big' supplies OS. The tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The tripos is the final honours examination for a Cambridge BA, so it is a set of major tests.

clue.text: Corruption riddled Victorian project

indicators.note: something riddled with a flaw has it running all through it, so it sits inside

parts.note: Victorian in its sense of prim and prudish
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century building scheme was full of graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun for a scheme but is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out beyond a surface, which is the verb sense of project.

clue.text: Autocrat created a scare

indicators.note: something created is made from its material in a new form

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictator caused a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became the title of Roman emperors, so it stands for an absolute ruler or despot.

clue.text: It's essential for weakling to keep a small coin

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a basic element

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within

parts.note: a runt is the weakest of a litter
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A puny fellow must always carry some loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic principle or first element of a subject, something fundamental to it.

clue.text: Oriental plant festival

parts.note: E for east
an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A celebration of flowers from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental' tempts you to take EAST, but then only the letters ER remain; it gives just E.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast celebrating the resurrection of Jesus, held in spring.

clue.text: Supporter for a girl in depression

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the girl is set in the hollow, inside it

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
a girl is referred to as her

explanation.surface: A fan offers help to a young woman who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood but is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower who sticks to a cause or leader, so the word is a synonym for a backer.
